section: Kakatiyas - origins, Beta I, Rudradeva, Ganapatideva; Kakatiya-Yadava-Hoysala relations
subsections: Capitals → which ruler shifted Hanumakonda to Orugallu

accepted.s: The ancient name ‘Orugallu’, associated with the later Kakatiya capital, literally means:
accepted.x: Orugallu is the ancient name of Warangal and means ‘single rock’.
accepted.tq: Use the exact meaning of the place-name rather than its later political association.
accepted.sec: Capitals → which ruler shifted Hanumakonda to Orugallu

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the names associated with the Kakatiya capital:
1. Andhranagari was a name used for Orugallu under Ganapatideva.
2. Sultanpur was the name given to Orugallu after the conquest of 1323.
3. Orugallu was the early capital made by Prola I.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Andhranagari was used under Ganapatideva, and Sultanpur was the name given after the conquest of 1323. The early capital was Anumakonda or Hanamkonda, not Orugallu.
accepted.tq: Split the statements by distinguishing the successive names and stages of the capital.
accepted.sec: Capitals → which ruler shifted Hanumakonda to Orugallu

accepted.s: With reference to the development of the Kakatiya capital, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Prola I — made Orugallu the capital
Rudradeva — gave Orugallu the name Sultanpur
accepted.x: Prola II developed Hanamkonda. Prola I made Anumakonda the capital, Rudradeva shifted the capital to Orugallu, and Sultanpur was the post-1323 name.
accepted.tq: Match each ruler with the correct stage in the evolution of the capital.
accepted.sec: Capitals → which ruler shifted Hanumakonda to Orugallu

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the respective roles of Rudradeva and Ganapatideva in relation to Orugallu?
o: Rudradeva began fortifying Orugallu, while Ganapatideva completed it and fully moved the court there.
Ganapatideva shifted the capital to Orugallu, while Rudradeva renamed it Sultanpur.
Rudradeva abandoned Orugallu, while Ganapatideva restored Hanamkonda as the capital.
Rudradeva completed the city and Ganapatideva began its fortification.
accepted.x: Rudradeva shifted the capital and began fortifying Orugallu. Ganapatideva completed the city and fully transferred the court there.
accepted.tq: Separate the initiating ruler from the ruler who completed the work.
accepted.sec: Capitals → which ruler shifted Hanumakonda to Orugallu

accepted.s: Who is identified as the first person named in the Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava dated 956 CE?
accepted.x: Kakartya Gundana is the first Kakatiya name in the Magallu grant of Danarnava dated 956 CE.
accepted.tq: Test the earliest named figure through the inscription-date association.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Beta I is correct?
o: He was known as Garuda Beta and obtained Anumakonda Vishaya through his aunt Viriyala Kamasani.
He invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva.
He was known as Arigajakesari and built Kesamudram tank.
He founded Orugallu and composed Nitisara.
accepted.x: Beta I, also called Garuda Beta, obtained Anumakonda Vishaya through his aunt Viriyala Kamasani. The other achievements belong to Prola I, Rudradeva and Mahadeva respectively.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler-achievement association and reject deeds belonging to neighbouring rulers.

accepted.s: Beta I attacked Kanchi in 1051 in support of which ruler?
accepted.x: Beta I attacked Kanchi in 1051 in support of Someshwara I.
accepted.tq: Link the military action to its stated political patron.

accepted.s: Who built the Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram?
accepted.x: Naranayya, the minister of Beta I, built the Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘minister–construction’ association without swapping ministers between rulers.

accepted.s: Prola I is associated with which combination of titles and achievement?
o: Arigajakesari; Samadhigata Panchamahasabda; construction of Kesamudram tank
Cholachamu Vari Pramathana; Vidyabhushana; construction of the Thousand Pillar Temple
Vidyabhushana; Kanchi Churakara; construction of Arikesari Samudram
Samadhigata Panchamahasabda; Rayagaja Kesari; construction of Ramappa temple
accepted.x: Prola I bore the titles Arigajakesari and Samadhigata Panchamahasabda and built Kesamudram tank.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure title and verify the achievement attached to the same ruler.

accepted.s: Which change is associated with Prola I during the development of the Kakatiya polity?
o: The capital changed from Orugallu to Anumakonda.
The emblem changed from Varaha to Garuda.
The capital changed from Hanamkonda to Kanchi.
The emblem changed from Garuda to Varaha.
accepted.x: During Prola I’s period, the Kakatiya emblem changed from Garuda to Varaha.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two directions of an emblem change.

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Beta II — Shivapura and Betesvaralayam
2. Durgaraja — donations to the Betesvara temple
3. Prola II — victory pillar at Srisailam
4. Mahadeva — construction of Ramappa temple
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Beta II built Shivapura and Betesvaralayam, Durgaraja made donations to the Betesvara temple, and Prola II erected a victory pillar at Srisailam. Ramappa temple belongs to the reign of Ganapatideva, not Mahadeva.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped ruler–achievement statement before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of which institution?
accepted.x: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of the Srisailam Mallikarjuna matha.
accepted.tq: Identify the religious teacher through the institution associated with him.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Prola II — victory pillar at Srisailam
accepted.x: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 belongs to Ganapatideva. Prola II is associated with Arikesari Samudram, the Swayambhu temple and the victory pillar at Srisailam.
accepted.tq: Find the achievement belonging to a different ruler.

accepted.s: Prola II was killed while fighting against which group?
accepted.x: Prola II was killed while fighting the Velanati kings.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the opponent in a ruler’s final military engagement.

accepted.s: Who, along with his wife Mailama, built the Jain Kadalalaya Jainavasadi at Anumakonda?
accepted.x: Chetanamatya, minister of Prola II, and his wife Mailama built the Jain Kadalalaya Jainavasadi at Anumakonda.
accepted.tq: Use the minister–spouse–monument linkage to avoid a ministerial name swap.

accepted.s: Rudradeva’s description as ‘Vidyabhushana’ is associated with which of the following?
o: His donations to the Betesvara temple
His independence from the Kalyani Chalukyas in 1163
His invasion of the Yadavas after the death of Mahadeva
accepted.x: Rudradeva was described as ‘Vidyabhushana’, and he declared independence in 1163, as recorded in the Thousand Pillar inscription.
accepted.tq: Connect the ruler’s title with the major political achievement of his reign.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Rudradeva:
1. He began the Thousand Pillar Temple tradition associated with Rudreshwara at Hanamkonda.
2. He founded Orugallu as the Kakatiya capital.
3. He was killed by the Yadava ruler Jaitugi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Rudradeva is associated with the Thousand Pillar Temple, the foundation of Orugallu as capital, and his death at the hands of Yadava Jaitugi.
accepted.tq: Check each achievement and the ruler responsible before choosing the inclusive code.

accepted.s: The Draksharamam inscription of 1158, attributed to minister Inangala Brahma Reddi, is important for its description of:
accepted.x: The Draksharamam inscription of 1158 describes the accession of Rudradeva and is attributed to minister Inangala Brahma Reddi.
accepted.tq: Pair the inscription date with the event it records.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Mahadeva is correct?
o: He built the Jain Kadalalaya at Anumakonda.
He invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva and died in battle while crossing a river on an elephant.
He issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244.
He founded Orugallu and completed its fortifications.
accepted.x: Mahadeva invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva and died in battle, reportedly on an elephant while crossing a river.
accepted.tq: Use the unusual detail of the ruler’s death to identify the correct statement.

accepted.s: Who was the guru of Mahadeva?
accepted.x: Dhruveshwara Pandita was the guru of Mahadeva.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Mahadeva’s guru from the religious teacher associated with Beta II.

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations relating to Ganapatideva is correctly matched?
o: 63-year reign; Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244; Ramappa temple built during his reign
44-year reign; Draksharamam inscription of 1158; Thousand Pillar Temple built during his reign
19-year reign; Bayyaram inscription; Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram
8-year reign; Kazipet Dargah inscription; Swayambhu temple built during his reign
accepted.x: Ganapatideva ruled for 63 years, issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244, and Ramappa temple was built during his reign by Recherla Rudra.
accepted.tq: Match the ruler with the period length, charter and monumental achievement.

accepted.s: Ramappa temple was built during the reign of Ganapatideva by:
accepted.x: Ramappa temple was built during Ganapatideva’s reign by Recherla Rudra in 1213.
accepted.tq: Separate the builder of the monument from ministers and inscription authors.

accepted.s: Which of the following set contains only works or grants associated with Ganapatideva’s reign?
o: Ramappa temple, Lakkavaram tank, Ghanapur tank and Ganapavaram villages
Arikesari Samudram, victory pillar at Srisailam and Betesvaralayam
Thousand Pillar Temple, Kadalalaya Jainavasadi and Kesamudram tank
Kesamudram tank, Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya and Swayambhu temple
accepted.x: Ramappa temple, the Lakkavaram and Ghanapur tanks, and the grant of Ganapavaram villages are associated with Ganapatideva’s reign.
accepted.tq: Eliminate sets containing achievements of different Kakatiya rulers.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Kakatiya rulers in chronological order of their reigns:
A. Prola II
B. Beta II
C. Rudradeva
D. Mahadeva
accepted.x: The order is Beta II (1076–1108), Prola II (1116–1157), Rudradeva (1158–1195), and Mahadeva (1195–1199).
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence using the beginning and end of each ruler’s reign.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
accepted.x: Ganapatideva ruled from 1199 to 1262. The periods given for Kakartya Gundana, Beta I and Prola I are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Check the numerical reign periods against the ruler sequence.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the ruler who united the Telugu lands and is regarded as the greatest Kakatiya ruler?
accepted.x: Ganapatideva is regarded as the greatest Kakatiya ruler and is credited with uniting the Telugu lands.
accepted.tq: Identify the ruler from the broad political achievement rather than a single monument.
